points.description: States that a linked list is a collection of elements (nodes/items linked together) that can be allocated dynamically (e.g., created at run time / size can grow or shrink, not fixed like an array).
points.partial_credit: Give 2-3 marks if only half is stated: either a collection/sequence of linked elements or nodes with no mention of dynamic allocation, or dynamic allocation with no mention of a collection of elements.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a linked list is a collection of elements (nodes) that is dynamically allocated or can grow and shrink at run time, in any wording, however brief. Part marks (2-3) if the answer gives only one half, such as nodes connected by pointers with no mention of dynamic allocation, or just 'dynamic' with no collection. Give 0-1 for answers that are unrelated or only name something else, like an array. Extra correct detail or minor wrong remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the core idea.
